title: Problem 08
markdown:
### Problem
In a triangle $ABC$, point $D$ is on side $BC$ with $CD = 2$ and $DB = 5$. Point $E$ is on side $AC$ with $CE = 1$ and $EA = 3$. Side $AB$ has length 8. The line segments $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $P$. Points $Q$ and $R$ lie on $AB$ so that $PQ$ is parallel to $CA$ and $PR$ is parallel to $CB$. Find the ratio of the area of triangle $PQR$ to the area of triangle $ABC$.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2025-p08](study/assets/asset-heuer-2025-p08-heuer-2025-p08.png)

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The ratio of the areas is $\frac{225}{676}$.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2025-p08-solution](study/assets/asset-heuer-2025-p08-solution-heuer-2025-p08-solution.png)

Since $PQ \parallel CA$ and $PR \parallel CB$, triangle $\triangle QRP$ is similar to triangle $\triangle ABC$.
The ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of any pair of corresponding sides:

$$\frac{\text{Area}(\triangle PQR)}{\text{Area}(\triangle ABC)} = \left( \frac{PQ}{AC} \right)^2.$$

We know $AC = CE + EA = 1 + 3 = 4$. We need to find the length of segment $PQ$.

Draw line segment $EK$ parallel to $AD$ with $K$ on segment $CD$.
In $\triangle ADC$, since $EK \parallel AD$:

$$\frac{KC}{DC} = \frac{EC}{AC} = \frac{1}{4} \implies KC = \frac{DC}{4} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}.$$

Then $BK = BC - KC = (5 + 2) - \frac{1}{2} = 7 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{13}{2}$.

Now in $\triangle BKE$, since $AD \parallel EK$ and $P$ is on $AD$, we have $DP \parallel KE$.
From similar triangles $\triangle BDP \sim \triangle BKE$:

$$\frac{BP}{BE} = \frac{BD}{BK} = \frac{5}{13/2} = \frac{10}{13}.$$

Next, in $\triangle BEA$, since $PQ \parallel AE$ (since $PQ \parallel CA$ and $E$ lies on $AC$):
Triangles $\triangle BPQ \sim \triangle BEA$ are similar, so:

$$\frac{PQ}{AE} = \frac{BP}{BE} = \frac{10}{13}.$$

Since $AE = 3$, we have:

$$PQ = \frac{10}{13} AE = \frac{10}{13} (3) = \frac{30}{13}.$$

Now compute the ratio of the areas:

$$\frac{\text{Area}(\triangle PQR)}{\text{Area}(\triangle ABC)} = \left( \frac{PQ}{AC} \right)^2 = \left( \frac{30/13}{4} \right)^2 = \left( \frac{30}{52} \right)^2 = \left( \frac{15}{26} \right)^2 = \frac{225}{676}.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Since sides of $\triangle PQR$ are parallel to sides of $\triangle ABC$, they are similar with area ratio $(PQ/AC)^2$. Auxiliary parallel $EK \parallel AD$ yields $BP/BE = 10/13$, so $PQ = \frac{10}{13} AE = 30/13$. With $AC = 4$, the ratio is $(15/26)^2 = 225/676$.

### Key Technique
Auxiliary parallel line construction to determine Menelaus cevial ratios and similar triangle area scaling.
